title: hunger for a creative feast, scorpio i
content:
this series is inspired by my collaboration with LJ of Ceremony for their communal writing practice, Atmospheres, based of the 36 decans of the astrological year.

Scorpio I — 23 October – 31 October
Key themes from LJ — hunger, the feast, indulgence
Before this: the eye of the storm, libra III

*

I drew this decan illustration while at an old friend’s wedding, before one of many nights of consecutive feasting. it made me think of how weddings are an archetypal container for community, celebration, a union of two beings that also has a Scorpionic violence inherent in its act of binding. intimacy is both rich and decadant, and its own kind of rupturing.

LJ wrote about the writing practice as a feast of its own — “Writing isn’t the fibre that balances our diet, it is the three-tier cake full of berries, narcotically delicious.”

I was really inspired by this way of relating to writing. I find that when I engage deeply in any creative practice, I’m coming face to face with my appetite for life. I long to relate to my practices with more of the illicit pleasure of midnight cake eating, instead of with the discipline routine of a cup of morning oatmeal. there is something about allowing ourselves to feel the hunger for a creative act — in all of its eroticism — so that, with anticipation, we can build up the energys towards a feast. in creative practice terms, this looks like a culmination into a project or creative sprint.

I want to continue keeping a pulse on my hunger for creativity, as a parallel to my hunger for pleasure, and darkness. it may not be necessary for me to stay functionally alive, but it is necessary to make me feel alive.

if making space for daily creative work isn’t about discipline, but about hunger, then the most crucial thing is to continually bring awareness to my own hunger; to play with hunger — as a way to build towards satiating it.
